# Parabolic Cylinder

![Parabolic Cylinder function icon](../../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/elliptic-parabolic-functions/02_Parabolic%20Cylinder.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../../../mathematics/index.md) · [All functions](../../../index.md)

Evaluates the normalized parabolic cylinder function Dv(x), the Weber solution with Dv(z)~z^v exp(-z*z/4) at positive infinity. v is a real order: negative and fractional values are accepted without rounding or abs(v). Exactly one output Dv(x), no derivative. D0(1)=D1(1)=.778800783071405; D2(0)=-1 and D2(1)=0; D0.5(1)=.842203244069840. Finite x and v define a real function; machine limits are diagnosed separately. Both inputs f64 required without defaults. ni_documented_real_v1 uses u=abs(x), never abs(k), abs(v) or abs(result); standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured.

## Studio authoring profile

Contract status: **partial**. The connector below describes Studio authoring; execution availability is stated separately.

<details>
<summary>Retained binding and help description</summary>

This is the source declaration, not the current measured product-execution assessment.

Evaluates the normalized parabolic cylinder function Dv(x), the Weber solution with Dv(z)~z^v exp(-z*z/4) at positive infinity. v is a real order: negative and fractional values are accepted without rounding or abs(v). Exactly one output Dv(x), no derivative. D0(1)=D1(1)=.778800783071405; D2(0)=-1 and D2(1)=0; D0.5(1)=.842203244069840. Finite x and v define a real function; machine limits are diagnosed separately. Versioned ni_documented_real_v1 evaluates at u=abs(x), normalizes -0 to +0 and preserves signed results. Only x is transformed; parameter k and real order v remain signed. Separate standard_real_v1 mathematical core keeps signed x. Profiles are fixed by the stable definition identity; no profile menu or silent migration. Both real f64 inputs are required without defaults. Jacobi returns separate cn, dn, sn and amplitude (phi in radians), in that exact order; Cylinder returns value Dv(x) only, with real nonintegral order v. Common NumericTreeMath extension promotes real numeric leaves to f64, preserves array rank/dimensions and ordered cluster fields, permits scalar/container lifting and requires exactly compatible container shapes. Jacobi produces four same-shaped outputs. Boolean, String, Path, references, error clusters, complex and Matrix are rejected. Native compiled provider is scalar f64 only. Existing FROG numerical diagnostics identify NaN input, domain, limit, overflow, underflow and nonconvergence. Precision limitations use the existing nonconvergence diagnostic, not a new precision_loss code. Highlight returns NaN with this diagnostic; the scalar native provider maps Nonconvergence to WorkLimit and aborts without partial publication. Domain errors do not change graph typing; no additional error or derivative terminal. Preserve nonzero representable subnormals and valid negative results.

</details>

## Types and connection rules

Both real f64 inputs are required without defaults. Jacobi returns separate cn, dn, sn and amplitude (phi in radians), in that exact order; Cylinder returns value Dv(x) only, with real nonintegral order v. Common NumericTreeMath extension promotes real numeric leaves to f64, preserves array rank/dimensions and ordered cluster fields, permits scalar/container lifting and requires exactly compatible container shapes. Jacobi produces four same-shaped outputs. Boolean, String, Path, references, error clusters, complex and Matrix are rejected. Native compiled provider is scalar f64 only.

- Type resolution: `custom_resolver`; result expression: `resolve:frog.studio.elliptic-parabolic-functions.type-resolution@1`.
- Implicit coercion: permitted by this profile.
- Arrays: accepted; lifting policy: `element_wise_same_shape_with_scalar_lift`.
- Shape rule: `preserve_rank_dimensions_and_ordered_fields; exact_container_shapes; four_same_shape_Jacobi_outputs`.
- Scalar lifting: yes.
- Broadcasting: no.

**Input count:** 2; this contract does not enable variadic inputs.

Port order: `argument` → `order`.
